description: We are OrbitX, a Cairo-based team passionate about space exploration, technology, programming, and innovation. We are building an interactive 3D map of Mars for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We love solving problems, learning new skills, and turning ideas into reality. Join us to gain experience, share ideas, and build something impactful. We welcome members interested in Python, JavaScript, 3D modeling, GIS, UI/UX, astronomy, research, and creative problem-solving.
summary: ORBITX: Mars Sentinel is a Google Earth–style Digital Twin of Mars, starting with Jezero Crater and built for the first human explorers. It ships as a game-grade Unity 6 desktop app and a Three.js Web twin, both fed by real NASA HiRISE/MOLA terrain, USGS SIM 3292 geology, and Perseverance, Curiosity, Ingenuity, MEDA and RAD data. Our Omni-Probe Planetary X-Ray lets users click any point (terrain, meteorite, habitat, Sun, Phobos, Deimos) to get coordinates, elevation, slope, geologic unit and a subsurface radar profile. A* routing finds the safest EVA paths, while dust-storm solar attenuation, radio line-of-sight, radiation alerts and closed-loop life support support autonomous crew decisions when Earth is up to 22 light-minutes away. Our vision: scale ORBITX into a planet-wide explorer for Mars, the Moon and beyond, one platform across 3D, Web and Game, open to scientists, crews and students.
details:
VISION

ORBITX aims to become the Google Earth of Mars: one living, explorable planetary platform delivered as a 3D simulation, a Web twin, and a Game-grade desktop app. Jezero Crater is our first fully built region, and the architecture is designed to expand to more Martian sites, the Moon, and other worlds

WHAT IT DOES

Earth is up to 22 light-minutes away from Mars, so astronauts must decide alone. ORBITX: Mars Sentinel gives them a layered 3D survival map:

1. Safest-route engine: hazard-weighted A* over real HiRISE (4 m) and USGS CTX (80 m) terrain. Safest route: 1,159.95 m, 6.49° max slope, 88.4/100 safety score. Shortest route: 1,113.50 m. Science route: 1,203.21 m linking Perseverance's cored sample tubes.

2. Omni-Probe Planetary X-Ray (creative highlight): click or walk to ANY terrain point, rock, meteorite, crater, habitat or celestial body (Sun, Phobos, Deimos, Earth) to instantly get Lat/Lon, MOLA elevation, slope, thermal inertia, USGS SIM 3292 geologic unit, RIMFAX-style subsurface profile (0–15 m) and PIXL/SHERLOC-style chemistry.

3. Survival physics: Beer-Lambert dust-storm solar attenuation (tau 0.45–2.80), dynamic Point-of-No-Return EVA radius, terrain-occluded radio line-of-sight, radiation alerts, 6x6 rover, 3 scout drones, closed-loop hydroponics and MOXIE O2.

IMPACT

Autonomous crew decision-making during communication blackouts, plus an engaging public tool for scientists, students and future mission planners. Every panel separates measured NASA/USGS data from simulated engineering physics, and documents terrain resolution assumptions.

TOOLS

Unity 6 (C#, URP, Cinemachine, InputSystem), Three.js (JavaScript, GLSL, WebAudio), Blender, Python data pipeline, SHA-256 integrity checks, 227 automated tests.

AI / SI ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

Code refactoring, coordinate validation, shader tuning and documentation formatting were assisted by the Antigravity AI coding assistant (Google DeepMind). All datasets, A* pathfinding, physics models and 3D builds were executed and verified by the team.
